name: Brainstem Architecture and Alternating Stroke Syndromes

reference.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students / Snell's Clinical Neuroanatomy
clinicalPearls: Pyramidal decussation in caudal medulla: 85% of corticospinal fibres cross to form lateral corticospinal tract

Lateral medullary (Wallenberg) syndrome: PICA occlusion damages nucleus ambiguus (dysphagia/hoarseness), spinal trigeminal (ipsilateral face numbness), spinothalamic (contralateral body numbness), sympathetic (Horner)
Medial medullary (Dejerine) syndrome: anterior spinal artery occlusion causes ipsilateral tongue paralysis (CN XII) and contralateral hemiparesis
Weber syndrome: paramedian midbrain branch occlusion causes ipsilateral CN III palsy with contralateral hemiparesis
Locked-in syndrome: basilar artery thrombosis infarcts bilateral ventral pons, sparing consciousness and vertical eye movements (CN III/IV in midbrain)
reference.pathophysiology: Brainstem alternating syndromes feature ipsilateral cranial nerve signs coupled with contralateral long tract motor or sensory deficits. Long tracts (corticospinal and spinothalamic) cross, while cranial nerve nuclei project ipsilaterally from their respective brainstem levels.
additionalInvestigations: Diffusion-weighted MRI (DWI) brain for acute posterior circulation infarction
CT angiography of head and neck for vertebral and basilar artery dissection or occlusion
Transcranial Doppler for posterior circulation hemodynamics
